item.content:encoded:
Israeli exit polls indicate deadlock in Tuesday's election Reuters | Updated: 28-10-2026 01:55 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 01:55 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Israel's election appeared to end in deadlock on Tuesday, exit polls showed, leaving neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot with a clear path to forming a government and raising the prospect of prolonged coalition bargaining or another election. The stalemate could work in Netanyahu's favour, allowing the prime minister to remain in power in a caretaker capacity while parties try to forge a governing coalition. Final results could take days, and Israel's fragmented political system leaves smaller parties potential kingmakers. No single party has ever won 61 seats outright in the 120-seat Knesset, making coalitions the norm. The vote drew record turnout as Israelis passed wartime judgment on Netanyahu in the first election since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Long lines formed outside polling stations as voters grappled with the trauma of Israel's deadliest day and the wars that followed. The policies of Netanyahu's right-wing coalition have been divisive at home and deepened Israel's international isolation, but he has portrayed himself as the leader with the mettle to face down Israel's foes. Netanyahu, 77, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents have managed to wrest the premiership from him only once since 2009, after four inconclusive elections in two years. Eighteen months later, he was back. He entered the election facing longstanding corruption charges, which he denies, and criticism over intelligence failures that allowed Hamas-led militants to kill 1,200 people and take 251 hostages. Eisenkot, 66, a hawkish former military chief who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, emerged as Netanyahu's strongest challenger, stressing his security credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically. He entered politics only four years ago and joined Netanyahu's war cabinet after the Hamas attack, but quit eight months later, criticising the prime minister's leadership. For many Netanyahu opponents, the election turned on accountability for the security failures of October 7. Opposition groups have promised a national inquiry, which Netanyahu has resisted. Netanyahu's nationalist brand of politics is deeply entrenched, and Israel's fragmented system makes it difficult for an array of opponents to force out his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties. Netanyahu had urged supporters to come out to vote to balance high turnout among his opponents on the left and Arab Israelis. "You all need to stream to the polls," he said. "This is a fateful moment." "I think these elections are the most important of all the ones I’ve known," said Ruth Epstein, an 81-year-old longtime left-wing voter in Ramat Gan near Tel Aviv, who voted for the opposition Democrats. Netanyahu campaigned on an endorsement from US President Donald Trump, his ally in the war against Iran, who has said they should "finish the job". (Additional reporting by Rami Ayyub in Jerusalem; Writing by Tom Perry and Michael Georgy; Editing by Howard Goller, Joe Bavier, Peter Graff and Kevin Liffey)

item.description: An AI-fueled tech rally sent US stocks to a higher close on Tuesday as third-quarter reporting season gained steam, while the Federal Reserve convened for its penultimate meeting of the year. The ...
item.content:encoded:
US STOCKS-Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum Reuters | Updated: 28-10-2026 01:52 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 01:52 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

An AI-fueled tech rally sent US stocks to a higher close on Tuesday as third-quarter reporting season gained steam, while the Federal Reserve convened for its penultimate meeting of the year. The tech-heavy Nasdaq led the gains. The buzz surrounding details of Anthropic's impending initial public offering helped boost chip stocks for the third consecutive session. Growing concerns over the viability of debt-funded spending amid rising borrowing costs have weighed on the AI trade this month. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index, while off more than 20% from its June 22 record closing high, has outperformed the broader market this year, gaining 62.1% compared with the S&P 500's 12.8% year-to-date advance. To fund its AI expansion, Meta increased its largest-ever equity fundraising to $97.5 billion, sending the Facebook parent's shares down 1.6%. "(The Anthropic news) seems to be giving a little bit of a relief rally to the AI stocks, particularly the semis," said Chuck Carlson, CEO at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana, referring to chip stocks. "Those stocks have gotten clobbered in recent weeks and they were probably due for a bounce." Economic data showed rising new orders for computers and peripheral equipment, supporting the notion of strong AI-related spending. Nearly half of S&P 500 companies have reported third-quarter results. Of those, 83% have delivered better-than-expected results, according to the most recent available LSEG data. Boeing tumbled 10.7% following its bigger-than-expected third-quarter loss, while water-management company Xylem slid 14.2% after trimming full-year forecasts. United Parcel Service advanced 5.8% after the package delivery firm raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts. Sherwin-Williams' quarterly profit miss sent the stock 2.7% lower, weighing on the Dow. Royal Caribbean rose 5.5% after the cruise operator lifted its full-year profit forecast. Microsoft and Alphabet results are expected on Wednesday, while Amazon.com is due to report on Thursday. The Fed convened on Tuesday for its October monetary policy meeting, which is widely expected to culminate in a decision to keep the fed funds target rate on hold in the 3.75% to 4% range, saving its second rate hike of the year for its final meeting in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool. "There seems to be more confidence that the Fed isn't going to do anything at this meeting, partly because we have an election on Tuesday," Carlson added. "There's probably at least some relief that the rate situation is not going to get in the way of a rally." The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 15.99 points, or 0.03%, to 52,377.57, the S&P 500 gained 45.83 points, or 0.60%, to 7,722.60 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 308.43 points, or 1.18%, to 26,477.81. Of the 11 major sectors in the S&P 500, technology led the gainers, while energy shares suffered the steepest percentage decline, hit by easing crude prices as attention turned to Middle East peace negotiations. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.83-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 81 new highs and 146 new lows on the NYSE. On the Nasdaq, 3,118 stocks rose and 1,680 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.86-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 11 new 52-week highs and six new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 62 new highs and 239 new lows. Volume on US exchanges was 16.10 billion shares, compared with the 17.18 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

item.content:encoded:
Kylian Mbappe issues apology after "ill-judged" remarks seemingly targeting Mao Zedong The controversy stemmed from a video of Mbappe's interview ahead of going on French online talk show 'The Bridge' circulating on X. In the video, Mbappe, often referred to as 'dictator' by fans for his influence on on-field action during matches, was asked about gus favourite meme, to which the superstar footballer replied that it was "a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator", before the video showed an altered image of Mbappe's face on Zedong's blue-suited body.  ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 22:47 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 22:47 IST

Kylian Mbappe (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

French and Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe has issued an apology for his comments, seemingly referring to Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China, after Chinese broadcasters pulled off coverage of Spanish league football, along with any matches featuring Mbappe, in response to his remarks, reported Goal.com. The controversy stemmed from a video of Mbappe's interview ahead of going on French online talk show 'The Bridge' circulating on X. In the video, Mbappe, often referred to as 'dictator' by fans for his influence on on-field action during matches, was asked about gus favourite meme, to which the superstar footballer replied that it was "a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator", before the video showed an altered image of Mbappe's face on Zedong's blue-suited body. Also, a prominent Chinese sports website, Dongqiudi, took a step in response to his remarks, deleting Mbappé's name from official ranking of the 2026 Ballon d'Or and replacing it with the phrase "chá wú cǐ rén", which roughly translates to "no such person exists" or "the person does not exist". Harry Kane, the English and Bayern Munich footballer, went on to win the Ballon d'Or, the highest individual award in football, while Mbappé finished second. Mbappe issued an apology on Tuesday on his social media. "During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself," he said. "My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurts many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history and I am sincerely sorry," the statement added. Javier Tebas, the president of La Liga, also issued an apology to the Chinese people on the association's behalf, posting on X, "We are aware of the harm this matter has caused, and I would like, on behalf of the Spanish league association, to offer our sincere apology to the Chinese people." He also warned of the fallout the incident could have caused for Spanish football regarding their fandom in China, saying, "We cannot allow an individual act to tarnish this relationship or harm more than 20 clubs that take part in our professional competitions, as well as millions of Chinese fans." (ANI)

item.title: Robert Pattinson calls Steven Soderbergh “completely selfless” for helping Matt Reeves finish ‘The Batman Part II’
item.description: Actor Robert Pattinson has praised filmmaker Steven Soderbergh for stepping in to help complete principal photography on ‘The Batman Part II’ while director Matt Reeves takes a temporary break from ...
item.content:encoded:
Robert Pattinson calls Steven Soderbergh “completely selfless” for helping Matt Reeves finish ‘The Batman Part II’ Actor Robert Pattinson has praised filmmaker Steven Soderbergh for stepping in to help complete principal photography on ‘The Batman Part II’ while director Matt Reeves takes a temporary break from filming due to a family matter, Variety reported.  ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 22:07 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 22:07 IST

Robert Pattinson (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Actor Robert Pattinson has praised filmmaker Steven Soderbergh for stepping in to help complete principal photography on ‘The Batman Part II’ while director Matt Reeves takes a temporary break from filming due to a family matter, Variety reported. In an interview, Pattinson expressed his gratitude to Soderbergh for offering to help Reeves complete the highly anticipated sequel, starring Pattinson as the iconic DC superhero Batman. “I am so happy he’s come on to help Matt," Pattinson said of Soderbergh. “It’s incredibly generous of him, and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless,” as per the outlet. The actor added that Reeves had invested considerable effort in the film’s script and that production was nearing completion. “I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great,” Pattinson said, according to Variety. When asked about the production schedule, Pattinson indicated that filming had already resumed. “I think they’re in production already. And I’m starting in a couple of days,” he said. Warner Bros. announced on October 5 that production on ‘The Batman Part II’ had been temporarily paused while Reeves focused on a family matter. The studio did not disclose further details about the circumstances. “Production on ‘The Batman Part II’ has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” a studio representative said at the time. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.” Reeves subsequently took to his X account to clarify that he remained the director of the film and expressed gratitude to Soderbergh for helping him complete the project. “Just to be clear, I am not leaving ‘The Batman Part II.’ I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes,” Reeves wrote, according to Variety. DC Studios co-chief James Gunn also addressed the change on Threads, reaffirming Reeves' position as director. “Matt is still the director of ‘The Batman 2’ and always will be. I can’t express how profoundly grateful and moved we are by Steven’s offer to help him complete his vision,” Gunn wrote. Soderbergh, meanwhile, said his objective was to ensure that the additional footage blended seamlessly with the material already filmed. “I thought Matt Reeves’ work on ‘The Batman’ was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent,” Soderbergh said. “The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.” ‘The Batman Part II’ is scheduled for release on February 18, 2028. No official announcement has been made regarding a change to the release date. Alongside Pattinson, the film features Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, Charles Dance, Brian Tyree Henry, Colin Farrell as the Penguin, Andy Serkis as Alfred Pennyworth and Jeffrey Wright as Commissioner Gordon, according to Variety. (ANI)
